note: Rewritten from Silvestri's Latin species-level description (Redia, pp. 41—43; archive.org identifier redia11903isti; species 16 in the original), covering the alate, soldier, worker, larva, nymph and supplementary reproductive worker, with all measurements. The original uses a comma as the decimal mark (e.g. 6,2, 4,5); here they are converted to a decimal point in accordance with Chinese usage, the values themselves being unchanged. Gaps in the OCR are not conjecturally filled: the hindwing value in the alate entry "Long. al. anter. 8,5, poster. 3" appears to have lost a figure (hence only the forewing, 8.5, is recorded in the text); the length of the nymphal wing buds (unreadable after "long. app." in the original) is not recorded; a few word forms are damaged (eeterum, auetum, Cerei, Kong. corp., etc.); the queen's "Long. corp. 27, lat. abdom. 5" is too large and the original probably read 2,7 and 0,5, but it is reproduced as it stands. The synonymy lines are recorded here as in the original: "Termes Strunckii W. Sor. Ent. Tidsk. V, p. 18. (1880)" and "Microcerotermes Strunckii Silv. (1901)". The generic characters, literature citations, figure numbers, localities (Patria: Colonia Benitez, Coxipò, Urucùm) and type-specimen records have been omitted. The author and year of this species appear in the source only in the synonymy lines above; the bibliographic item is in the registry file papers.json.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head and thorax blackish fuscous, rest of body chestnut; sternites 1—5 with a broad median band of dirty ochre yellow. Body with numerous hairs and some setae. Head nearly oval, without a fontanelle; ocelli very close to the eyes. Antennae 14-segmented, segment 3 the smallest and ring-like, segment 4 slightly longer than 3, segment 5 slightly longer than 4. Pronotum less than twice as wide as long, anterior angles rounded, posterior part considerably narrowed, posterior margin rounded and concave in the middle. Wings densely covered with minute 5—6-radiate papillae and with sparse hairs, the margins hairy; media of the forewing reaching the wing before the middle, complete or giving off 1—3 branches, submedia with 9—11 branches; media of the hindwing with 1—2 branches, submedia with 8—9 branches. Tibiae with 3 rather large apical spurs; cerci slightly thick. Measurements: body with wings 10 mm, body 6.2 mm; antenna 1.5 mm, head width 0.85 mm; pronotum length 0.5 mm, width 0.8 mm; forewing 8.5 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head ochreous ferruginous, anterior part rusty; mandibles black; rest of body straw yellow. Body hairs rather sparse, with some additional setae posteriorly. Head nearly rectangular, with a small lateral tubercle anteriorly and a fine narrow carina in the middle. Labrum 1/3 as long as the mandibles, anteriorly suboval. Mandibles long, strongly convergent at the base, slightly curved and pointed at the tip, inner margin edentate, only faintly marked with fine teeth. Antennae 15-segmented, segment 3 less than twice as long as segment 2, segment 4 about as long as 3, segment 5 only slightly longer than 4. Pronotum with only the anterior margin slightly upturned and rounded, concave in the middle, narrowed laterally, posterior margin nearly truncate. Measurements: body length 4.5 mm, mandible length 1.04 mm; head length 1.75 mm, width 1.04 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head chestnut, with pale transverse bands at the sutures; or head ochre yellow, densely covered above with large fuscous punctures; rest of body straw yellow, abdomen with dirty patches from food. Mandibular dentition smaller than in the alate. Antennae 13-segmented, segment 3 half as long as segment 2, segment 4 slightly longer than 3, segment 5 slightly longer than 4. Anterior part of the pronotum slightly upturned and rounded, middle slightly concave, posterior part slightly narrowed, posterior margin deeply concave. Sternite 7 small. Second cercal segment long and slender. Genital appendages very short. Measurements: body length 4.7 mm, abdominal width 1.3 mm, head width 0.9 mm.

sections.label: Nymph
sections.text: Nymph straw yellow, eyes black, wing buds long, body length 6.5 mm. Larva white, with short hairs; antennae 12-segmented, segments 3 and 4 bare, subequal and very small; body length 1.4 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Supplementary reproductive worker (female): head blackish chestnut, the sutures marked with fine ochre lines; upper surface pale yellowish brown, especially posteriorly, lower surface dirty straw yellow; sternite 7 sulphur yellow. Eyes absent. Antennae 15-segmented, segment 3 almost half as long as segment 2, segment 4 slightly longer than 3, segment 5 only slightly longer than 4. Anterior part of the pronotum slightly upturned and broadly rounded, angles rounded, posterior part trapezoidal. Sternite 7 large, its posterior margin very broadly rounded. Measurements: body length 4.7 mm, abdominal width 1.3 mm, head width 0.9 mm. Queen 27 mm long, abdominal width 5 mm. The author's supplementary notes on the Coxipó specimens: alate 9.6 mm with wings, soldier 4.6 mm, worker 5.2 mm.
